summary: Brattleboro water department's three-story wooden tower, built 1943 to watch its reservoir watershed; vandalism reports run to 1979; FFLA lists it standing.

facts.design: 34-foot three-story wooden tower; 12 ft square base, 10 ft second floor, 8 ft top deck; painted white with tar-shingle roof

staffing.status: manned part-time, mainly in dry spells

facts.agency: Brattleboro water department (built 1943); called a town-owned fire tower in 1973

events.note: Erected by the Brattleboro water department under Justin A. Holden; reported as completed except interior finishing in July 1943
Manned for some time during dry woods conditions, per October 1947 report
Reported as a town-owned fire tower; an electric meter at it was destroyed
Brattleboro Department of Public Works reported to police that the tower had been shot up; damage to door and telephone lines
Break-in and vandalism reported at the tower

sources.title: Pleasant Valley Reservoir (Forest Lookouts), quoting The Brattleboro Reformer 1943-1979

notes_for_editor: Build date 1943 and staffing come from 1943-1947 newspaper items transcribed on the Forest Lookouts page; not checked against the Reformer itself. The only current evidence of the tower is the FFLA 'Standing' entry; no recent condition or access report was found. Access is unknown: the site is town watershed land on Pleasant Valley Road, and no public-access rule was found, so no access level is recorded. Height is not given in metres because the 34-foot figure's reference point (ground or cab floor) is not stated. The record's kind 'three_story' and county Windham match the sources; no corrections proposed.
